definition: A debt security that is not HTM or trading; measured at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses (other than credit losses) in OCI.
A warranty that only assures the product meets agreed specifications; accrued as a cost, not a separate performance obligation.
Collected within the period or soon enough afterward (generally 60 days for property taxes) to pay current-period liabilities.
Income available to common shareholders divided by the weighted-average common shares outstanding.
An exchange changes the entity's future cash flows significantly; determines whether gains on nonmonetary exchanges are recognized.
Operations and cash flows clearly distinguishable from the rest of the entity; the unit for discontinued-operations reporting.
An existing condition with an uncertain outcome that will be resolved by a future event (e.g., litigation).
An entity's obligation to transfer goods or services for which it has received (or is owed) consideration — deferred revenue.
Expected lifetime credit losses on financial assets at amortized cost, recognized through an allowance.
Future tax savings from deductible temporary differences and carryforwards, measured at enacted rates.
Future taxes payable from taxable temporary differences, measured at enacted rates.
EPS that includes all dilutive potential common shares (if-converted and treasury stock methods).
A disposal of a component that represents a strategic shift with a major effect on operations and results.
Interest = carrying amount × market rate at issuance; the difference from cash is amortization.
Investment adjusted for the investor's share of investee income and dividends; used with significant influence (generally 20–50%).
The price received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date (exit price).
A lease meeting any of the five classification criteria; the lessee recognizes interest and ROU amortization separately.
The excess of consideration plus NCI fair value over the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired; tested for impairment, not amortized (public).
A debt security the entity has the positive intent and ability to hold to maturity; carried at amortized cost.
A quoted price in an active market for identical assets or liabilities.
An unobservable input reflecting the entity's own assumptions.
The governmental-fund basis: revenue when measurable and available; expenditures generally when the liability is incurred.
NFP net assets subject to donor-imposed time or purpose restrictions, or perpetual restrictions.
Estimated selling price less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal, and transportation.
The equity in a subsidiary not attributable to the parent, reported within consolidated equity.
A lease meeting none of the finance-lease criteria; the lessee recognizes a single straight-line lease cost.
Changes in equity from nonowner sources excluded from net income (e.g., AFS debt fair value changes, translation adjustments).
A promise to transfer a distinct good or service (or a series) to the customer.
Correction of an error in previously issued statements, made to beginning retained earnings.
An event after the balance sheet date that provides evidence about conditions that existed at that date (Type I).
An affiliate, principal owner, management, immediate family, or any party that can significantly influence the other.
An operating segment that meets a 10% revenue, profit/loss, or asset test (or is aggregated or chosen to reach 75%).
A lessee's right to use an underlying asset over the lease term.
The price at which an entity would sell a promised good or service separately; the basis for allocating the transaction price.
A difference between an item's tax basis and its reported amount that will produce taxable or deductible amounts in future years.
The entity's own shares reacquired and not retired; a contra-equity account.
A contra-DTA for the portion of a deferred tax asset that is more likely than not to go unrealized.
Consideration that can vary (discounts, bonuses, penalties); estimated by expected value or most likely amount, subject to the constraint.
